# Licence log

**Generated — do not edit by hand.** Run `npm run check:licences` to regenerate.

This is the pre-publication due-diligence record for every asset on disk. Per **D12b**
this project imports everything each atlas offers, remains open source, and renders every
attribution its sources require; this file is how the licence position stays knowable
rather than assumed. Structure counts are read out of the shipped GLBs, not from a
hand-maintained table, so they cannot drift from what actually ships.

Project stance: **open source, non-commercial, fully attributed — the twin will be published under an open licence with every required credit rendered in-app and embedded in each asset. Non-commercial components (CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA) are therefore compatible with the intended use, and the obligation they carry is attribution plus not selling it. ⚠️ One exception the stance cannot cover: geometry with NO licence statement grants nothing at all, so it needs written permission rather than a credit line.**.

## Assets

- **Licence:** Apache-2.0

- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Structures:** 3
- **Required credit:** Beating biventricular heart from biv-me (UOA Heart Mechanics Research), Apache-2.0 — a model fitted to one subject's cine MRI, 25 cardiac phases.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present

### `public/models/eye.glb`

- **Licence:** None required — generated by this project
- **Source:** scripts/build-eye.mjs
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Structures:** 3
- **Required credit:** Schematic optical eye generated by open-twin-openXR from the published Arizona eye model (Schwiegerling). Geometry original to this project.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** THE ONLY ASSET HERE WITH NO UPSTREAM RIGHTS HOLDER. Generated from published radii, conic constants, thicknesses and refractive indices. Those are measurements, and measurements are not copyrightable expression, so the mesh is ours outright — no licence, no attribution chain, no provenance question. Crediting Schwiegerling for the parameters is courtesy and good scholarship, not a licence condition. This is the pattern to reach for whenever a structure is fully specified in the literature: generate it and own it.

### `public/models/htb-ct-003.glb`

- **Licence:** CC BY 4.0
- **Source:** https://www.cancerimagingarchive.net/collection/healthy-total-body-cts/
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Required credit:** Segmentations from the TCIA Healthy-Total-Body-CTs collection (subject 003), CC BY 4.0; meshed for this project. doi:10.7937/NC7Z-4F76.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** The first complete FEMALE body in this repo, and the first atlas derived from a real person's CT rather than modelled. Verified at source rather than from a survey: the segmentations AND the clinical demographics are both CC BY 4.0, and only the CT images sit behind the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy -- which does not matter, because the images are not needed to build this. Subject 003 is F, 26, 1.7018 m, BMI 20.4, from the collection's own clinical spreadsheet. Closes ROADMAP Phase 6, which HRA could not: HRA's female donor has no skeleton above the pelvis.

### `public/models/openear-zeta.glb`

- **Licence:** CC BY 4.0
- **Source:** https://zenodo.org/record/1473724
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Required credit:** OpenEar library of 3D models of the human temporal bone (Sieber et al., MED-EL / University of Bern), CC BY 4.0. Surface colour baked from the same specimen's true-colour micro-slicing volume.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** The D4 texture pilot at 1/100th of Visible Human's cost (B3), and it ANSWERS D4: photographic tissue colour does survive this pipeline. The first asset here coloured by what the tissue looked like rather than by a palette we chose. Licence re-confirmed CC BY 4.0 from the Zenodo API. Specimen ZETA only, indexed and pulled member-by-member over HTTP range requests by scripts/remote-zip-index.mjs, which fetched 140 MB instead of 7.3 GB. Meshes are in RAS and the colour volume in LPS, so the shipped FlipXY.h5 — diag(-1,-1,1) — is the whole registration: 6,985 of 7,200 sampled vertices land inside the volume on non-black tissue. Placed by landmark fit rather than by eye — five structures common to it and Z-Anatomy, 1.27 mm RMS, and the same fit is what identified it as a RIGHT ear.

### `public/models/z-anatomy-regions.ao.glb`

- **Licence:** CC BY-SA 4.0
- **Source:** https://github.com/LluisV/Z-Anatomy
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Structures:** 257
- **Required credit:** Z-Anatomy - The open source atlas of anatomy - CC-BY-SA 4.0; derived from BodyParts3D - The Database Center for Life Science - CC-BY-SA 2.1 Japan.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** Surface topography from Regions of human body100.fbx — 256 named regions of the body surface. Plain CC BY-SA with none of the three third-party components, so it is the cleanest asset in the set. A SEPARATE GLB for a geometric reason, not a licence one: the patches lie on the skin and would occlude every organ if merged into z-anatomy.

### `public/models/z-anatomy.ao.glb`

- **Licence:** CC BY-SA 4.0 aggregate, incl. CC BY-NC-SA and CC BY-NC components and one component with no licence
- **Source:** https://github.com/LluisV/Z-Anatomy
- **Loaded by the app:** yes
- **Structures:** 3,614
- **Required credit:** Z-Anatomy - The open source atlas of anatomy - CC-BY-SA 4.0; incl. Anatomy of the Inner Ear by University of Dundee School of Medicine (CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0), Kidney by lissiecowley (CC-BY-NC 4.0), and Brainder/white matter by University of Washington (NO LICENCE STATED); derived from BodyParts3D - The Database Center for Life Science - CC-BY-SA 2.1 Japan.
- **Embedded `asset.copyright`:** ✅ present
- **Why:** All seven system files imported (D12b). Per-structure component tags live in the asset's own structure table, so docs/LICENCE_LOG.md counts what actually ships. THE SHIPPED BUILD IS THE --publishable ONE: 3,614 structures, of which 3,606 are Z-Anatomy's own CC BY-SA work and 8 come from two non-commercial components (4 Dundee inner ear, 4 lissiecowley kidney). The 3 unlicensed University of Washington white-matter structures are excluded by --publishable and are NOT in it. The full research build is 3,617. Both differ from the 3,626 quoted before a zero-vertex-part guard stopped emitting nine empty structures, and from the 8-structure Dundee tag before the inner-ear pattern was narrowed to exclude the middle ear.

Third-party components inside this asset:

| structures | licence | component | rights holder |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 4 | CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 | Anatomy of the Inner Ear | University of Dundee School of Medicine |
| 4 | CC BY-NC 4.0 | Kidney | lissiecowley |
| 3606 | CC BY-SA 4.0 | Z-Anatomy's own geometry | Z-Anatomy authors |

- **Anatomy of the Inner Ear:** Non-commercial and share-alike. Attribution is required and is rendered by AttributionBar. The sense organ only — the cochlear and vestibular NERVES and NUCLEI are Z-Anatomy’s own and are not tagged.
- **Kidney:** Non-commercial. Attribution required.

## Not usable at any point

Recorded so nobody re-investigates them. These are closed by **contract or price**, which
no decision of ours can relax — unlike a licence choice, which is ours to make.

| source | instrument | why |
|---|---|---|
| zygote | proprietary, five figures | Terms forbid redistributing the content or 3D derivatives. Not reachable by D12 — this is a contract and a purchase, not a licence tier. |
| uk-biobank | material transfer agreement | Signed MTA forbids sublicensing and redistribution, and derived results return to the holder. A decision of ours cannot relax an agreement with someone else. |
| nako | material transfer agreement | As UK Biobank. |

## Action list before publishing

- [ ] **public/models/ct-atlas-f.glb** carries no `asset.copyright` — the credit is not travelling with the file.
- [ ] **bodyparts3d**: DBCLS have not confirmed the relicence in writing. Chase it before relying on the CC BY reading for anything that matters.
- [ ] **z-anatomy**: ⚠️ DISTRIBUTION GATE: the University of Washington white-matter component (3 structures) has NO licence statement, and serving to logged-in users is still distribution — a login wall does not change this. Build with `npm run build:z-anatomy -- --publishable`, which drops exactly that component and keeps the non-commercial ones (they need attribution, not removal). See docs/DEPLOY.md. The permanent fix is written permission or CT-segmented white matter from MOOSE (Apache-2.0).
- [ ] **ct-atlas-f**: If the pipeline is ever re-run with TotalSegmentator's GATED subtasks (tissue_types, appendicular_bones, face), the output becomes tier 2 and needs its own id here — the academic weights licence is non-commercial.
- [ ] **htb-ct-f**: Nothing outstanding on rights. Two properties must travel with any use of it, both recorded in docs/healthy-total-body-cts-crosswalk.tsv. Labels are GROUPED -- one Ribcage rather than 24 ribs, one Spine rather than 24 vertebrae, every long bone merging left and right -- and the images being restricted means it cannot be re-segmented finer. And it is low-dose non-contrast CT, so bone is trustworthy and soft tissue is not: D10's contrast objection applies to the organ masks. ⚠️ Do not re-run this with TotalSegmentator's gated subtasks; that would make the output non-commercial and it would need its own entry.
- [ ] **biv-heart**: ⚠️ BLOCKS PUBLICATION — and the question is now PRECISE rather than a suspicion. Resolved by reading the upstream repo and the FIMH 2025 paper (doi:10.1007/978-3-031-94562-5_34) on 29 July 2026: the paper's own acknowledgements thank 'the study participants of the UK Biobank and CARDIOHANCE', and the abstract says the pipeline was tested on CMR data from TWO CENTRES. So UK Biobank involvement is established fact, not an inference from Steffen Petersen's co-authorship. The repo still carries NO data statement, no ethics or consent text, and it bundles input DICOMs under demo/dicoms for a case named 'patient1'. THE ONE OPEN QUESTION: which of the two cohorts is patient1? If UK Biobank, redistribution of derived geometry is almost certainly barred by their access terms — derived data returns to UK Biobank and is not published onward — and Apache-2.0 at the repo root cannot override the authors' own obligations. If CARDIOHANCE (Auckland), it turns on that study's consent and ethics approval, which the authors know and we cannot. ASK: joshua.dillon@auckland.ac.nz (corresponding author, Auckland Bioengineering Institute) and charlene.1.mauger@kcl.ac.uk (KCL) — both listed as contacts in the repo README. If the answer is UK Biobank or otherwise restricted, replace with the Sunnybrook CC0 fitted models (docs/INTEGRATION_CANDIDATES.md C3), which carry no such question. Draft email in docs/PLAN_INTEGRATION.md under B6.
- [ ] **schematic-eye**: Nothing to verify for rights. What DOES need saying every time it is shown: it is a SCHEMATIC OPTICAL model — cornea, lens and retina only, with no sclera, iris, ciliary body, extraocular muscles, optic nerve or vasculature. Correct as optics; not a substitute for an anatomical eye, and not a donor's.
- [ ] **openear-zeta**: Nothing outstanding on rights, and the pipeline blocker is fixed: all 12 structures now carry baked photographic colour, and it renders as the `openear` organ overlay. Three properties travel with any use of it. It is ONE cadaveric RIGHT temporal bone, not a population. 71.5% of its surface has a colour source and the rest is neutral grey, because the micro-sliced block (~39.6 x 39.6 x 51.8 mm) is smaller than the scan -- grey means 'no source', never 'this colour', and the per-structure split is in the asset's own extras. And it is ~14% larger than Z-Anatomy's inner ear, left unscaled deliberately; see the note in src/scene/organOverlays.ts.
- [ ] **inter-font**: RESOLVED — no external runtime fetch remains. Verified twice: no fonts.googleapis or fonts.gstatic reference in src/ or index.html, and a full network capture of the running app shows every request on localhost with /fonts/InterVariable.woff2 served 200. Kept as a record because re-adding a CDN font link would silently reopen a GDPR exposure — LG Muenchen I (3 O 17493/20) held the IP disclosure alone sufficient. The only characters that still fall back are the emoji and geometric icons Inter genuinely lacks, which is correct: self-hosting an emoji font is neither wanted nor generally licensed.
- [ ] **npm-runtime**: Re-run the checker after any dependency bump. The one historical trap is @pmndrs/assets (CC0, fine) pulling a re-resolution of the whole pmndrs stack.
